page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance engineered for workloads demanding high memory density relative to core count. The server is built on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache pool. Supported instruction extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while AVX-512 extensions and AMX units are absent. The configuration does not include local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage and standard remote interfaces.

System memory consists of 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a generous 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid execution across computational and data-intensive tasks. In compute profiling, the instance achieved strong top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core (2726.67) and multi-core (64784.93) tests, as well as in the overall PassMark CPU score (51331.69) and PassMark encryption test (51361.84). Memory benchmarks reflect a PassMark memory score of 2903.87 in the top 25%, with cached 16 KB read bandwidth reaching 3109.12 GB/sec and uncached 256 MB reads and writes achieving 83.85 GB/sec and 53.29 GB/sec, respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performed in the upper quartile at 222.56 GB/sec.

Performance remains in the middle range for standard web serving (29.17 GB/sec), Redis SET commands (47.32 million operations per second), PassMark database queries (19905.02), and Clang compilation (34417.0). Large language model text generation degrades noticeably as model parameters scale, yielding 282.34 tokens per second on lightweight 135M models but declining to a bottom-decile 2.31 tokens per second on 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators.

Qualitatively, the E48as_v5 offers favorable resource efficiency for enterprise deployments requiring large working sets in memory without paying the premium associated with discrete GPU compute. However, the total absence of bundled local NVMe storage means all persistent data and fast caching rely entirely on remote managed disks, requiring consideration of network I/O limits. The server is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, data analytics pipelines, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E48as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 24-core AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the system targets large-footprint enterprise services, though it includes no local disk storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark results reflect strong computational throughput in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark encryption evaluations, paired with competitive cached memory bandwidth. Tasks such as static web serving, Redis operations, and medium-scale model inference perform within median ranges, while large 70B parameter LLM inference is limited by CPU execution speeds. The E48as_v5 offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy setups where local NVMe is unnecessary, making it suitable for in-memory databases, business intelligence caching layers, enterprise backend services, and multi-threaded analytical batch processing pipelines.

tagline: A high-capacity memory-optimized server powered by AMD EPYC processors, providing 384 GB of RAM for demanding enterprise memory workloads.
bullet_points: 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor (24 physical cores at 3.525 GHz)
384.0 GB system RAM providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory-to-core allocation
Strong multi-core compute and encryption performance in stress-ng and PassMark benchmarks
Zero bundled local disk storage, requiring external Azure managed storage volumes
Absence of GPU acceleration, resulting in limited throughput on large parameter LLM generation
Well suited for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and large memory batch processing
